info.title: devctl reservation and Kubernetes gateway API
info.description: Whole-cluster reservations through one stable /k8s gateway, with a full CLI and browser UI. Administrator booking limits, durable primary selection and activity-based inactivity expiry apply across devices. Browser or CLI-issued opaque PATs have editable server-side automatic-booking preferences, disabled by default. An existing primary always wins. Only an explicitly enabled valid PAT can allocate on a gateway request when no primary exists, choosing a matching entirely unused live nonmaintenance cluster transactionally. Login, setup, creation/editing preferences and token refresh never allocate. Original Kubernetes credentials stay encrypted server-side. The standalone kubectl subcommand client was removed.

patch.summary: Update maintenance or placement labels without changing existing bookings
patch.description: Administrator only; requires an audit reason. Optional maintenance and labels fields form one atomic update. labels replaces the entire registry label map, including labels:{} to clear it, and requires expected_labels containing the previously loaded label map. A stale snapshot returns409 with reload guidance rather than overwriting another editor. Labels accept at most32 Kubernetes-qualified keys and string values (empty values are valid). Omitted fields are preserved; explicit nulls, duplicate label keys and non-string values are rejected. Label edits are permitted while a cluster is occupied or in maintenance. They affect future UI/CLI/PAT placement only: active bookings, primary selections, PAT policies/expiry, sharing and upstream credentials are unchanged. No Kubernetes API call is made. Same-value updates with a current snapshot succeed without duplicate success audits; retired/unknown IDs return404. Unexpected persistence failures return503 without database details.

401.description: Invalid access token or unapproved user

403.description: Administrator or owner permission required

409.description: Loaded labels no longer match current metadata; reload current labels, review changes and retry

parameters.description: Required with browser cookie authentication, together with exact Origin. Not required with explicit Bearer JWT.

maintenance.description: Pause or enable new placement without evicting current holders.

labels.description: Full replacement devctl registry labels, not Kubernetes object labels. Keys follow Kubernetes qualified-label syntax (optional DNS prefix); values may be empty strings. An empty object clears all labels.

expected_labels.description: Required with labels: exact previously loaded map for optimistic concurrency. {} represents no labels. Legacy snapshots may contain old invalid metadata so administrators can repair it; only the replacement must satisfy current label rules.

reason.description: Nonblank audit reason, trimmed before persistence; maximum1000 UTF-8 bytes.

delete.summary: Deregister an unused cluster and remove its stored kubeconfig
delete.description: Administrator only; an audit reason is required. Rejects409 while any active booking holds the cluster, including shared bookings. First stop/release bookings or let legitimate inactivity expiry finish; there is no force-deregister option. Transactionally removes encrypted upstream credentials and placement visibility while retaining public archived metadata, booking history, creation idempotency records and audit events. Never contacts Kubernetes, deletes workloads or revokes upstream credentials or PATs. Retired cluster IDs cannot be reused; display names can be reused by a new ID. Repeating deregistration of an archived ID succeeds without duplicate audit; unknown IDs return404.

get.summary: Forward a Kubernetes API request to the authenticated developer’s current primary
get.description: Stable catch-all Kubernetes API gateway, not a remote shell endpoint. Validates a trusted API JWT or developer-scoped opaque PAT, resolves the current owned active primary from server state, and pins this request to its reservation and selection version. No primary with automatic booking disabled returns403 text/plain with “no cluster is booked”, preserving the message in native typed/raw kubectl clients. Other gateway rejections use Kubernetes Status JSON as documented. JWT and manual-only PAT requests never allocate. An explicitly enabled valid PAT with no current primary can transactionally book a matching unused cluster, assign primary and forward the request. No match returns403 text/plain with an actionable capacity/selector explanation; it never joins shared holders or chooses outside the rule. Streams recheck credential validity, active reservation and unchanged primary; a switch closes old streams rather than migrating them. JWT streams can continue through fresh authenticated primary heartbeats during actual activity. PAT streams recheck PAT expiry/revocation separately. Original upstream credentials remain server-side, caller identity headers are stripped, verified upstream HTTPS uses HTTP/1.1 for WebSocket/SPDY, and Kubernetes content/status/queries are preserved. Browser cookies never authenticate this route. Accepted requests and still-authorized open streams extend only this primary booking’s inactivity deadline. Automated API clients count as activity. Release preserves upstream workloads and PATs.

200.description: Upstream Kubernetes response; content type and status are preserved. Watch/log responses may stream.

101.description: Bidirectional upgraded Kubernetes stream (for example WebSocket/SPDY), passed through by the gateway.

401.description: Invalid or expired API JWT / personal token.

403.description: No primary with automatic booking disabled, unavailable matching automatic capacity or booking-limit failure returns text/plain with an actionable message. Other gateway authorization denials return Kubernetes Status JSON.

text/plain.example: no cluster is booked; book a cluster in the web UI or with devctl start

409.description: Primary selection changed or booking ended during routing; retry the command. This is distinct from the no-primary text403 response.

default.description: Other upstream Kubernetes statuses and response content are passed through, including resource-specific errors. Do not assume all upstream responses are JSON.

post.summary: Record foreground interaction on the exact owned primary

200.description: Current reservation with computed inactivity deadline

401.description: Invalid or expired API token / unapproved identity

403.description: Owner, administrator or browser CSRF permission required

409.description: Booking limit, unavailable cluster, ended/foreign selection or no active primary conflict

post.description: Authenticated presence assertion used by visible browser UI after actual input. It is not proof of human presence. Exact booking ID and selection version prevent a stale tab from extending a newly selected cluster. Server supplies timestamps and inactivity policy; no client duration, expiry or timestamp accepted. Throttled to 15s persistence; cannot revive an expired booking. Browser cookie requests require Origin and CSRF. PATs cannot call this control endpoint.

parameters.name: X-CSRF-Token
parameters.description: Required with browser cookie authentication and the exact configured Origin. Not required with an explicit Bearer JWT.

bearerAuth.description: Trusted issuer, API audience, valid signature and expiry, explicit access-token marker and approved group required. ID tokens rejected.

browserSession.name: __Host-devctl-web
browserSession.description: Opaque Secure HttpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie; OAuth credentials remain encrypted server-side. Cookie-authenticated POST/PATCH/DELETE require the exact configured Origin and X-CSRF-Token from /web/session. Cookies never authenticate Kubernetes gateway requests.

personalToken.description: Opaque dcpat_ credential accepted only by /k8s. Uses its developer’s current primary; if absent, only an explicitly enabled PAT can reserve a matching unused cluster from its saved preferences. Cannot call control/admin APIs, edit policy, switch an existing primary, refresh itself or extend its fixed expiry. Default8h/max168h; individually revocable; survives logout.

expires_at.description: Server-computed inactivity auto-release deadline, advanced by accepted activity. Required for active reservations; not a fixed booking duration.

last_activity_at.description: Last persisted accepted primary Kubernetes request, authorized open stream observation, explicit selection or foreground browser interaction signal. Writes are throttled to 15s. Polling and OAuth heartbeats do not count.

primary.description: Whether this active booking is its owner’s current primary. First booking is selected automatically; later bookings do not switch it.

deregistered_at.description: Present on archived metadata returned for historical session details. Deregistered clusters never appear in current registry/availability lists, have no stored kubeconfig and cannot be selected or booked.

Booking.description: Explicit whole-cluster booking. Auto-release deadline derives from administrator inactivity policy; client booking inactivity deadlines are rejected.

id.description: Stable ID, unique across current and deregistered records. Use a new ID when registering again after deregistration.

name.description: Display name, unique among currently registered clusters; retired names can be reused.

labels.description: Initial registry labels with at most32 Kubernetes-qualified keys and string values. Empty values are permitted. These labels guide future reservation placement; no Kubernetes label is modified.

kubeconfig.description: Administrator-only import of one portable context with static embedded token or certificate/key and verified HTTPS. Encrypted immediately, used only by the backend transport, and never returned to developers.

server.description: Stable configured public HTTPS origin plus /k8s. It contains no session, binding or developer identifier. The authenticated identity determines the primary cluster on the backend; setup does not reserve a cluster.

certificate_authority_data.description: Optional base64-encoded public PEM CA data for gateway TLS, never upstream client credentials.

scope.description: New credentials use kubernetes:primary. Historical legacy credentials may be listed with a different scope and are revoked during migration.

PersonalAccessToken.description: Public metadata only, including current automatic-booking preferences. No digest or token is returned. Existing/issued PATs default disabled. Token validity and fixed expiry are independent of booking inactivity deadlines and policy edits.

ttl.description: 1m through168h, default8h. Independent of reservation inactivity deadline; no sliding renewal.

kubeconfig.description: Sensitive one-time gateway-only YAML containing stable /k8s URL, public trust metadata and opaque PAT. The same file survives later preference edits, primary changes and new bookings until fixed PAT expiry or explicit revocation. Preferences are stored server-side and no new download is needed.

owner_id.description: Stable ownership key derived from trusted issuer plus subject; never email.

max_bookings.description: Effective identity-wide maximum active bookings, including shared bookings.

max_bookings_override.description: Optional administrator override. Absence means inherit the current global default.

primary_session.description: Current owned active primary, omitted when no booking exists.

selection_version.description: Changes when the primary changes; gateway streams remain pinned to the version they started with.

inactivity_grace_period.description: Go duration in whole seconds, 1m through 168h. Applied to each booking independently from its last activity or initial baseline.

cluster.description: An owned active cluster ID, display name, or booking ID.

authorization_expires_at.description: OAuth authorization lease for this exact primary version, bounded by verified JWT expiry. Gateway additionally enforces the independently moving inactivity deadline and current selection; token refresh alone does not extend a booking.

enabled.description: Explicit opt-in to label-based allocation on a gateway request if no owned primary exists.

selector.description: Equality labels using Kubernetes qualified-key/value syntax. Every pair must match. Empty values require the label to exist with that value. Empty map permits any unused cluster.

AutoBookingPolicy.description: Mutable server-side placement preferences bound to a PAT record, not embedded arbitrary kubeconfig metadata. Complete replacement on PATCH; omitted selector clears it. Changes affect future allocations only and preserve token, expiry, file and existing primary.

reason.description: Audit reason; required when an administrator edits another developer’s credential. Owner edits use a default reason if omitted.
